title: Let old wrong codes age out instead of closing a later pairing window
before: 4 wrong codes, +4 days, open window, 1 wrong -> window closed (window_open False)
after: window stays open; its own 5th wrong code still closes it; two windows each close on their own 5th
note: per-window code_misses on each OPEN window; lifetime _wrong_codes removed; unmatched codes with no window open count against nothing

title: Promote and erase rewrite write-once memories that replication cannot carry
before: promote rewrote A's file in place, B kept the stamped copy; after erase a cursor-reset pull brought X back to A and B kept X
after: B serves a core successor (never the stamped copy, core or project); B holds no row/file of X; re-pair brings none back; B's later note untouched; 2nd pull leaves fingerprints equal
note: ADR 0234 at e6063806. Promote = core successor (supersedes+promoted_from); erase = retired erased:<spc> tombstone, receiver erases created<=it, ErasedRefused blocks re-pull. Promote now mints a new id

title: Project erase removes the project's receipts runs file
before: erase unlinks linked cases to core (ADR 0225, tests/spaces/test_routes.py:153); case keeps 20 receipts, goals/<proj>.runs.txt keeps the rest; runs_archived counts it
after: not built: deleting it drops receipts of a chore that survives, and its footer would count M receipts that no longer exist
note: Premise false: no erase deletes a case (no case-delete path exists). ADR 0233 'move, never drop'. If cases get a delete, the runs file goes with that, not with a space erase
